sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, a 20.5% CAGR to $155.2 billion, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, revenue up 17.8% and operating income up 20.8%, driven by Microsoft Cloud and Azure [D472][D473][P17].
FY2023 was the soft year, revenue growth of 6.9% as More Personal Computing declined on Windows and Devices [D311][P39].
Microsoft Cloud reached $214.4 billion, 64.6% of revenue, and contributed 16.2pp of FY2026's growth [S24][D566][D568].
Server products and cloud services rose 31.5% to $129.4 billion, 39.0% of revenue, on Azure demand across all workloads [S61][D640][D641][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added $14.2 billion, up 16.2%, on Copilot and E5 revenue per user [S64][D648][P14].
Operating costs grew 7.4% against 17.8% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 53.3% [D491][D472][D498].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against 31.3% net income growth, with the share count down only 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as AI infrastructure investment raised cost of revenue [D486][F30][D981][P11].
Cost of revenue took 0.9pp off operating margin in FY2026, while R&D and other lines added 0.8pp and 1.2pp [D500][D501][D502].
The FY2026 net margin jump of 4.2pp to 40.3% came largely from $10.7 billion of other income, including OpenAI dilution gains [D488][F70][X124][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, 55.1% of revenue, on higher customer cash and lower tax payments [F100][D477][D457][P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, a 20.2% margin and window low, as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion [F120][D478][D456][D982][F110][D479].
Free cash flow covered only 0.50x of net income, against a 0.91x median, and capex ran 3.38x D&A [D460][D990][D461].
The capex step-up reflects AI infrastructure build-out, with investing outflow of $139.5 billion including $51.4 billion more property additions [F130][P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, with total debt down to $40.3 billion [D465][D466][D464].
That net cash position ranks in the 83rd percentile of six software peers, whose median is -7.2% of revenue [D1006][D1007].
Buybacks and dividends of $48.7 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow [D467][D468].
The current ratio of 1.23x is a window low against a 1.93x median, as current liabilities compounded at 13.1% [F200][D991][D993][F233].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the lowest in the window [R1][D406][D460][D988].
This is a capital-intensity signal rather than an earnings-quality one, since operating cash flow still covered net income 1.37x [D459].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, so FY2017 comparisons use first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
Product revenue members overlap and sum to 180% of FY2026 revenue, so they should not be added [R5].
If free cash flow margin stays below the 20.2% FY2026 low as capex runs above $115.9 billion, the cash-conversion trend worsens [D982][F110].
A Microsoft Cloud share below the 64.6% FY2026 level, or growth under the 26.9% pace, would mark a slowdown in the main driver [D566][D567].
Operating margin falling back toward the 41.7% median would reverse the leverage trend; watch it in the FY2027 10-K [D975].
